groups.defect: The async legacy writes in Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection take their timeout context from the request ctx, which is cancelled when the handler returns, so legacy writes get cancelled and the stores diverge. Legacy errors are also never logged, and the new mode-3 playlist integration tests that read legacy right away are racy.
groups.rationale: All four report the same request-context cancellation problem in the background legacy goroutines, with the same WithoutCancel fix. Some members also mention the missing error logging and the racy integration tests.

groups.defect: Metrics are recorded with the wrong helper or label: Create (line 45) and Update (line 129) send storage failures to recordLegacyDuration, the legacy DeleteCollection call (line 166) uses recordStorageDuration, and the Delete success path (line 106) passes name instead of kind. Delete (line 97) also puts d.Log into the context instead of the enriched log.
groups.rationale: s_74e86eb7 reports all of these mix-ups, including the Delete logger. Each other member reports one or more of them, so the overlap chain links them into one group.

groups.defect: Legacy Update gets the raw objInfo instead of an updateWrapper around the object that unified storage produced, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge or fail.
groups.rationale: All three point at the same lines with the same missing updateWrapper and the same fix.

groups.defect: The Create goroutine passes the shared obj pointer to Legacy.Create while the same object may be mutated or serialized elsewhere, causing a data race. Fix: use DeepCopyObject.
groups.rationale: Both report the same shared-object data race in Create and propose the same deep-copy fix.
